bio:
A native Chicagoan, O’Shaughnessy lived for 28 years in the Wicker Park neighborhood, where she started Wood Street Gallery. It was off the beaten path, which she saw as a challenge to getting people to come see art. Her focus was emerging Chicago artists, those with potential, who hadn’t had any gallery shows. A combination of themed group and solo shows brought people out to the neighborhood. Having 5,000 square feet, there was an opportunity to have up to 5 individual shows a month. 

O’Shaughnessy, and her husband, Charlie Van Gilder, both artists, sold their building in Chicago in 2014, and made the decision to move to Port Townsend, where Van Gilder had lived in the late 70’s and early 80’s. Since then, they have been focusing on their own art.

O’Shaughnessy decided in 2021 that she wanted to expand her studio from the small room she’d been working in and build a studio where she could get back to making sculpture. As she planned it, the idea for a gallery attached to the studio seemed the right thing to do. She wanted to recreate what she had accomplished in Chicago, having a place to help the creative artists on the peninsula show their work.
name: Aurora Loop Gallery

bio: Art exploration, or process art, is a creative endeavor that focuses on the process of art making, rather than the production of an end result. bio: I am an Eco-Dietitian, Educator and Nutrition and Sustainability Advisor who is bringing my passion for jazzy/funky/hip-hop-esque dancing to Port Townsend, WA. I have  been embracing “Dance Club” moves for close to a decade and have studied dance at Westlake Dance Center and Exit Space Dance Studio in Seattle, and studied privately with Jason Umbao. My first career was in the theater which included performances in shows like Cabaret, Little Shop of Horrors.  I don’t pretend to be any kind of advanced professional dancer but I do love dancing and dancing with others.  I bring a high energy, but low key, low pressure and supportive vibe to my classes where everyone, (including me!), is invited to be themselves and shake it like they mean it.

bio: Feral Fine Arts began with one person’s journey to rediscover the wild within themself. While backpacking for a year throughout New Zealand, Myco rediscovered one of their most important senses. The sense of touch. As they felt their way back into their wild ways, they studied weaving with plants, animal fibers, felting, and spinning. This affirmed their lifelong fervent pursuit of all things fiber arts. They sold their work abroad and began teaching fiber arts to all ages.
name: Feral Fine Arts

The Turret Journal
bio: The Turret Journal is written by Zhenya Lavy from the Adams Pragge House, 1028 Tyler Street, Port Townsend, Washington. This journal attends to the continuing life of this house — not only its structure and materials, but also its light and lived experience across seasons — as well as its place within Port Townsend and at the northeastern tip of the Olympic Peninsula. It is also an act of recovery — of the people who lived here, loved here, and shaped the civic, cultural, and national life of their time, and whose connection to this house has been largely forgotten.
